summary: First-finish smoke test for LicenzPol. Backend endpoints and full frontend E2E purchase flow verified against public URL. Everything working; one minor spec inconsistency (slug 'software-made-simple' referenced in review does not exist in catalog).
passed: GET /api/products -> 31 items in {total,items} envelope with realistic brands (Windows, Office, Nero, Norton, etc)
GET /api/products with filters (category=os, brand=Microsoft, platform=Windows, license_type=Perpetua, need=work, q=windows, sort=price_asc/desc, min_price/max_price) returns filtered/sorted subsets
GET /api/products/windows-11-pro -> full product incl. variants, features, activation, faq (200)
GET /api/related/windows-11-pro returns related products in same category
Home page loads with nav, hero-cta-catalog, cart button
Category filter filter-cat-os narrows to 4 cards
Product detail page opens with add-to-cart-button and add-to-compare-button
Add to cart opens drawer; cart-checkout-btn navigates to /checkout
Checkout step 1 form (email/first_name/last_name/country) advances via checkout-next-1
Checkout step 2 confirm-order creates order and displays order-reference (LP-A844A276) on success screen
No console/page errors during E2E flow

failed.issue: Review references slug 'software-made-simple' for product detail/related endpoints but no such product exists in catalog.py (only real software slugs). Tested with 'windows-11-pro' instead; both success and 404 semantics work.
failed.evidence: GET /api/products/software-made-simple -> 404; catalog has slugs like windows-11-pro, office-2021-professional-plus, norton-360-deluxe, etc.

action_items: None blocking for first-finish. Consider clarifying/aligning the 'software-made-simple' slug used in test IDs vs the actual catalog if that was intended as a real product.

notes.mocked: Order creation is a DEMO by design (no real payment gateway). POST /api/orders returns demo=true and status=demo_confirmed.
notes.credentials: None required (guest checkout). /app/memory/test_credentials.md is empty which is expected.
